item.title: ESA downplays Space Rider test mishap
item.description: The European Space Agency acknowledged it lost a test article for its Space Rider spaceplane in a recent drop test but said the mishap would not significantly delay its development.

item.title: Space Force shifts missile-warning, cislunar missions from Vulcan to Falcon Heavy
item.description: Three GPS launches, an SDA mission and two higher-energy missions moved from Vulcan to SpaceX rockets. ULA will receive later SpaceX payloads in return.

item.title: NASA’s Swift space telescope ends mission
item.description: NASA has shut down an astronomy spacecraft in a decaying orbit after a failed attempt to reboost it with a commercial spacecraft.

item.title: China launches highly retrograde Yaogan-50 spy satellite, Long March 4B lofts six further Yaogan spacecraft
item.description: HELSINKI — China conducted a pair of launches Friday, first sending a new retrograde spy bird into orbit, and following up with two sets of Yaogan triplets.

item.title: NASA keeps options open to preserve 2028 Artemis lunar landing
item.description: NASA officials say they are keeping open options regarding launch vehicles and landers to preserve a crewed lunar landing in 2028, even while noting Artemis 3 remains behind schedule.

item.title: Space Force looks to build depth into its satellite-jamming arsenal
item.description: Lt. Gen. Gagnon says units need more equipment to absorb wartime losses

item.title: Nov. 5: Satellite Mission Management at the Edge
item.description: Join us to explore how emerging technologies and commercial capabilities are transforming satellite operations

item.title: ESA says Ariane 6 engine issues resolved
item.description: The European Space Agency says engine issues that have delayed Ariane 6 launches have been resolved as it continues to study ways to increase the vehicle’s flight rate.

item.title: Pentagon looking past Earth orbit for its next military frontier
item.description: Military officials are describing the vast region between Earth and the moon as a future battlefield. The Space Force is starting to put acquisition plans behind the rhetoric.

item.title: Turning capacity into capability: recommendations for America’s ground station infrastructure.
item.description: The commercial space industry is rapidly adding ground station capacity around the world. This collective investment will lower the cost of antenna access, increase supply and lower prices — but counterintuitively, more antenna capacity does not necessarily translate to capability across the diverse landscape of satellite operators and missions.

item.title: NASA advisers raise new concerns about Artemis lunar landing plans
item.description: Ahead of a NASA update on its Artemis lunar exploration plans, the agency’s safety advisers expressed concerns about the maturity of those plans.

item.title: HawkEye 360 launches six satellites to expand customer-dedicated intelligence services
item.description: SpaceX and Rocket Lab missions bring the company's constellation to 39 satellites as it expands a business model built around multiyear customer commitments

item.title: New launch pads set to boost China’s Hainan commercial spaceport
item.description: HELSINKI — China’s first commercial launch site is set to bring two new pads online by end of year, targeting more than 30 launches in 2027.

item.title: China seeks payloads for crewed moon lander test mission
item.description: HELSINKI — China is seeking payloads to fly on an uncrewed mission of its Lanyue human moon landing system, ahead of a planned crewed landing before 2030.
